articles.title: Tucker Carlson claims Trump mulling nuclear attack on Iran
articles.summary: Tucker Carlson claimed late Sunday that the Trump administration could launch a nuclear strike on Iran within days, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is press...
articles.full_text:
Tucker Carlson claimed late Sunday that the Trump administration could launch a nuclear strike on Iran within days, alleging that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressuring President Donald Trump to authorize an attack on a suspected nuclear site in central Iran.
In a lengthy post on X, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believes Iran has resumed its nuclear enrichment program.
Carlson is a conservative political commentator and former Fox News host whose program, Tucker Carlson Tonight, aired from 2016 to 2023.
He now hosts an independent political show on X, where he regularly comments on U.S. foreign policy and international affairs.
Carlson claimed conventional U.S. weapons could not penetrate the estimated 91.44 meters (300 feet) of solid granite protecting underground tunnels at the site, leaving a nuclear strike as the only military option.
"Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day," Carlson quoted an unnamed informed observer as saying.
Carlson argued that Netanyahu's political survival is driving his push for further military action. He claimed Netanyahu needs Trump's intervention to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset following the latest election results, warning that otherwise he could lose power and face investigations and possible imprisonment.
He also alleged that Netanyahu has been pressing senior U.S. officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper, to resume major combat operations.
Carlson also claimed that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe were following Netanyahu's lead.
He further said former President Barack Obama had also opposed the Iran peace agreement being drafted in Doha.
Carlson said U.S. allies in the Middle East were increasingly concerned about renewed fighting. He claimed Netanyahu secretly traveled to Abu Dhabi on Sept. 27 to persuade the UAE to support a final attack on Iran, but Emirati officials refused.
Warning of the economic consequences, Carlson said eight months of conflict had severely affected Gulf economies, as well as global energy and fertilizer markets. He claimed 11 of the world's approximately 850 oil supertankers were badly damaged in the Strait of Hormuz in October alone.
He also warned that a nuclear explosion at Pickaxe Mountain could contaminate the Gulf and threaten the water supply of around 100 million people.
Carlson argued that a U.S. nuclear strike could establish a dangerous precedent, potentially encouraging Russia to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine, triggering renewed nuclear tensions between India and Pakistan, and prompting North Korea to attack Seoul.
"After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable. That war would be short and final," he wrote.
He further alleged that the Trump administration had quietly revised U.S. nuclear doctrine since February to make the first use of so-called "battlefield nukes" easier and more likely.
Carlson said Trump could decide by Nov. 7 whether to authorize the use of nuclear weapons, adding that Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff were urging him to pursue a diplomatic agreement with Tehran.
Although acknowledging that negotiations would be difficult, Carlson said people who had spoken with Iranian decision-makers believed there was a consensus that further conflict would benefit no one and that an agreement was worth pursuing.
He concluded by warning that the consequences of a nuclear strike would extend far beyond Iran, arguing that the international public had been excluded from decisions that could threaten millions of lives.
"Now would be the time for them to speak up," Carlson wrote.
Carlson's claims follow Trump's remarks to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida Saturday that one or two Iranian nuclear facilities remained potential targets and that the U.S. could strike them within 10 minutes.
Trump specifically mentioned Pickaxe Mountain, saying he had military plans for the area, but did not indicate that a nuclear strike had been authorized.
"You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly," he added.
In an Oct. 16 interview with Newsmax, he explicitly ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran.
Separately, Axios reported that Trump and Netanyahu held a tense phone call Saturday, citing Israeli and U.S. sources. According to the report, Netanyahu is pushing for renewed military action immediately after Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections, while Trump prefers to allow diplomatic negotiations to continue.
A White House official said the administration does not comment on sensitive military plans, adding that Trump is keeping all options open to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.
Secretary of State Rubio has also said no final decision has been made on resuming strikes.
Iran, meanwhile, denies any nuclear activity at the Pickaxe Mountain complex. Its supreme leader has warned Washington and Tel Aviv against launching further attacks.

articles.title: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz in 2 days as draft US deal circulates
articles.summary: Iran said Monday it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington met its demands, as an official briefed on Qatari-mediated talks said a draft proposal to end th...
articles.full_text:
Iran said Monday it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington met its demands, as an official briefed on Qatari-mediated talks said a draft proposal to end the war with the U.S. was being circulated.
Iranian negotiators left Doha earlier Sunday, though their departure was not due to difficulties in the negotiations, the official told Reuters. A follow-up meeting was possible, they said, without providing details of the draft.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi had visited Doha to facilitate exchanges with Washington through Qatari intermediaries.
Baghaei added that the talks were based on a seven-step proposal Iran put forward in September to reopen Hormuz and end the U.S. naval blockade on Iran. Tehran now says the plan could be implemented more quickly.
"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," he said.
"We have stated that, if Iran's demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period."
Baghaei said messages were still being exchanged through mediators and that "everything depends" on Washington accepting Tehran’s demands.
"Only then can we discuss the subsequent stages."
Iran’s conditions include ending the Middle East war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets abroad, lifting sanctions on its oil sector and ending the U.S. naval blockade.
"Our demands have been articulated very clearly and transparently. These demands are reasonable and logical: no final agreement can be initiated, nor can the Strait of Hormuz be reopened or secured, unless the U.S. naval blockade is brought to an end, Iran's demands are respected, and Iran's legitimate requirements are addressed," Baghaei said.
The September proposal, conveyed to Washington through Qatar, envisaged a seven-day process, with the strait reopening on the sixth day after the United States met Iranian demands. President Donald Trump rejected the initial proposal.
In an interview with Al Jazeera, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Hormuz could reopen within two days under an agreement.
He also said Washington must accept a new transit route through the strait agreed upon by Iran and Oman, remove sanctions imposed in recent months and reduce U.S. troop numbers in the region.
Since the Middle East war began in late February, Iran has claimed control over Hormuz, a vital shipping passage for global energy supplies and regularly targeted vessels attempting to cross without its authorization. Washington imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports in response.
Since August, the United States has also imposed a new round of sanctions as part of what it called the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran.
The diplomatic exchanges come amid concerns that fighting could escalate after Tuesday’s U.S. midterm elections. The United States and Israel have intensified threats in recent days to renew attacks on Iran amid crucial elections in both countries.
Trump has said Washington would not launch new attacks before the U.S. vote and described talks with Tehran as productive, though he has not ruled out further military action.
On Saturday, Trump said he still had to "take care" of one or two targets, including Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site. Tehran denies it is a nuclear facility.
Baghaei warned Monday that Iran would retaliate against any renewed attack.
"Any act of aggression against Iran, any military attack against Iran, by whatever means, will be met with a powerful, immediate and comprehensive response from us," he said.
Asked about the U.S. midterms, Baghaei said Tehran did not expect the elections to "give birth to a new U.S."

articles.title: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of undermining Israeli election results
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party Monday of seeking to discredit the country's parliamentary election results, a...
articles.full_text:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party Monday of seeking to discredit the country's parliamentary election results, alleging a deliberate campaign to undermine public confidence in the electoral process.
"Likud and Netanyahu are fighting to contain their losses and are continuing, with full force, a destructive and violent attack aimed at delegitimizing the election results and the Central Elections Committee,” Eisenkot wrote on X.
He said the campaign highlighted "the grave danger” posed by Netanyahu and Likud retaining their grip on centers of power and government.
Eisenkot described the attacks as a refuge for those who understood the scale of their defeat.
"They have grown accustomed to acting as they please, without limits or constraints, but those days are over,” he added.
His remarks followed Likud’s demand for an urgent meeting of the Central Elections Committee to discuss suspicions of foreign interference before the final results are certified.
Responding Monday evening, committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg said the results would be published as scheduled, according to daily Israel Hayom.
Netanyahu and right-wing parties in his bloc have alleged fraud and manipulation in voting within Israel’s Arab community during last Tuesday’s election.
The dispute comes ahead of President Isaac Herzog’s consultations with parliamentary factions, scheduled to begin Wednesday and continue Thursday, before he selects a lawmaker to task with forming a government.
Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for the Jewish opposition parties and 19 for the Arab parties.
Eisenkot has the backing of the 48 opposition lawmakers after the Democrats, Together and Yisrael Beytenu decided to recommend him for the mandate.
The two Arab lists are also expected to recommend Eisenkot, potentially raising his total to 67 recommendations and strengthening his prospects of being selected.
Receiving the mandate, however, would not guarantee that he could assemble a governing coalition.
Under Israel’s Basic Law: The Government, the designated lawmaker has 28 days to form a government, with a possible presidential extension of up to 14 days.

articles.title: Deal with Iran to end war could happen, Trump says
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran was seeking an agreement to end the war with Washington, expressing optimism that a diplomatic breakthrough could be reached. He d...
articles.full_text:
U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran was seeking an agreement to end the war with Washington, expressing optimism that a diplomatic breakthrough could be reached.
He did not immediately provide details.
Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.
A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. U.S. President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran.
The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the U.S. lifting its blockade on Iran's ports.
They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American, and in one case Israeli, officials.
One official said Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the U.S. administration to persuade Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.
Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.
Other U.S. allies in the Middle East are warning against more strikes, saying it would destabilize the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.

articles.title: German police foil suspected neo-Nazi attack on refugee shelter
articles.summary: German police prevented a suspected arson attack by neo-Nazi extremists targeting a refugee shelter in northern Germany, authorities said Monday. A 15-year-old suspect is in pretri...
articles.full_text:
German police prevented a suspected arson attack by neo-Nazi extremists targeting a refugee shelter in northern Germany, authorities said Monday.
A 15-year-old suspect is in pretrial detention on charges that include preparing a terrorist act, public broadcaster NDR reported, citing authorities.
The Lueneburg prosecutor's office confirmed that police had searched the homes of two suspects, who were under investigation for allegedly conspiring to commit arson.
Police detained the teenager after witnesses reported seeing him walking through a town carrying a gasoline canister.
Investigators found that the incident coincided with the date mentioned in online chats as the planned time for an arson attack on a refugee shelter in Winsen, in the northern state of Lower Saxony.
The chats reportedly involved young neo-Nazis discussing plans to attack the shelter on a Friday night.
The Flensburg prosecutor's office said Monday that the 15-year-old remained in custody.
Beyond the suspected arson conspiracy, investigators accused the teenager of preparing a serious terrorist act and expressed concern that he could commit similar offenses if released.

articles.title: US contacts signal recognition of Tehran's 'victory': Iran VP
articles.summary: Iran's vice president said indirect exchanges with the United States signaled recognition of Tehran's "victory," as President Masoud Pezeshkian announced Monday that Supreme Leader...
articles.full_text:
Iran's vice president said indirect exchanges with the United States signaled recognition of Tehran's "victory," as President Masoud Pezeshkian announced Monday that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had granted the government additional authority to pursue negotiations aimed at ending the Middle East war.
"Our enemy failed to achieve any of its objectives in the last two wars. Even today, although the United States, driven by its own goals and concerns regarding domestic public opinion, is engaging in various maneuvers, the messages conveyed to Iran through intermediaries point to an acknowledgment of our victory," said Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref, according to IRNA state news agency.
The vice president's remarks presented the ongoing diplomatic contacts as a sign of Iran's success, even as Tehran and Washington continued communicating through regional mediators amid concerns over renewed hostilities.
Pezeshkian said the Iranian government was working toward a diplomatic resolution and had received additional powers from the supreme leader to advance the process.
"We are striving to resolve the issue through dialogue. In this regard, the Supreme Leader has also conferred certain powers on the government," Pezeshkian was quoted as saying by the official IRNA news agency.
His comments followed confirmation from Iran's Foreign Ministry that Tehran and Washington were exchanging messages through intermediaries as diplomatic efforts continued to prevent the conflict from escalating again.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that indirect discussions with the United States were particularly intensive, with Qatar and Pakistan playing prominent roles in facilitating communication.
"Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive. Qatar and Pakistan are playing a very active mediating role in these negotiations," Araghchi said in a video interview with IRNA.
The statements highlighted Tehran's efforts to present its diplomatic engagement with Washington as consistent with its position in the conflict, while keeping channels open for a negotiated settlement.
Iranian officials did not specify the extent of the authority granted to the government or indicate whether the latest exchanges had resulted in concrete progress toward an agreement.
The diplomatic contacts come amid continuing uncertainty over the future of the Middle East conflict, with regional mediators seeking to prevent a renewed outbreak of fighting.

articles.title: Israel's expansionist policy ‘biggest threat’ to region: Jordan’s king
articles.summary: Jordan’s King Abdullah II said Monday that Israel’s expansionist ambitions pose the greatest threat to the region’s future, stressing that regional security and stability cannot be...
articles.full_text:
Jordan’s King Abdullah II said Monday that Israel’s expansionist ambitions pose the greatest threat to the region’s future, stressing that regional security and stability cannot be achieved without Palestinians securing their rights to their land.
"Israeli expansionist ambitions remain the greatest threat to the region’s future and its hopes," Abdullah said in a speech to parliament.
He pointed to the continuing humanitarian catastrophe in the Gaza Strip and Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, despite international calls to halt Israeli violations.
He stressed that there could be no security or stability in the region without recognizing the Palestinian people’s rights to their land.
"We reiterate, time and again, that there can be no security or stability in our region without upholding the Palestinian people's right to their homeland," he said at the opening of Jordan's parliament.
Jordan neighbors Israel and the occupied West Bank. It has long advocated for a two-state solution and signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994.
"Those who believe tyranny grants legitimacy are mistaken, and those who believe time erases the truth are mistaken," the king said.
The speech came days after Israel held a legislative election which saw Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party win the most votes, but still fall short of a majority.
He reaffirmed Jordan’s commitment to its principles, Arab identity and defending Arab causes, pledging to maintain that position as his father had before him and his son would after him.
The monarch also stressed that achieving a unified Arab position would remain a priority for Jordan.
Israel has waged a genocidal war on Gaza since October 2023, killing more than 74,500 Palestinians and injuring over 175,000 others, most of them women and children.
Israeli military operations and attacks by illegal occupiers have also intensified in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem.

articles.title: Israeli strikes kill 3 in Gaza as 4th Palestinian dies of wounds
articles.summary: Israeli strikes killed three Palestinians and wounded 10 others in the Gaza Strip Monday, while a fourth Palestinian died of wounds sustained in an attack the previous day, accordi...
articles.full_text:
Israeli strikes killed three Palestinians and wounded 10 others in the Gaza Strip Monday, while a fourth Palestinian died of wounds sustained in an attack the previous day, according to medical sources.
A man was killed and five others, including a woman and two girls, were wounded in a strike in al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, a medical source at Nasser Medical Complex told Türkiye's Anadolu Agency (AA). Witnesses said an Israeli drone fired at least one missile toward a Palestinian in the area.
Another strike in Khan Younis killed a Palestinian man and wounded four others, one critically, the medical source said.
In central Gaza, a 40-year-old man was killed and another Palestinian was moderately wounded in an Israeli attack east of Deir al-Balah. Medics cited by Reuters identified the location of the fatal strike as al-Masdar.
A fourth Palestinian man died Monday of wounds sustained in an Israeli strike on al-Mawasi Sunday afternoon.
The Israeli military said it carried out two strikes targeting Palestinian resistance members but provided no further details.
Witnesses also reported that an Israeli quadcopter dropped a bomb on a gathering of Palestinians east of al-Masdar village, east of Deir al-Balah. They said Israeli forces demolished homes and buildings outside their deployment areas east of the village.
Israeli military vehicles and bulldozers have entered the area in recent days amid heavy gunfire and artillery shelling, according to local sources. They said the destruction of homes and civilian structures had forced several families to flee.
Military vehicles also opened heavy fire toward areas east and south of Khan Younis, local sources and witnesses said.
In Gaza City, witnesses reported artillery shelling and gunfire from Israeli military vehicles toward eastern neighborhoods, while Israeli naval vessels opened fire toward the coastline.
Israel has stepped up strikes in recent weeks, accusing Hamas of rearming and launching attacks in violation of a year-old cease-fire. Hamas denies trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the agreement.
Israeli attacks have killed 1,583 Palestinians and wounded 5,711 others since the cease-fire took effect on Oct. 10, 2025, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry. Israel says four soldiers died during that period.
The U.S.-brokered agreement calls for the eventual reconstruction of Gaza, but negotiators have made little progress toward agreeing on terms for Hamas to disarm or Israel to withdraw its troops.
Israeli forces control about two-thirds of the territory after ordering residents out of those areas. Nearly all of Gaza’s more than 2 million residents live in the remaining third, which remains under Hamas’ effective control, mostly in makeshift tents and damaged buildings amid the ruins.
Israel’s genocidal war has killed more than 74,500 Palestinians and wounded more than 175,000 others since October 2023, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.
The war was triggered by the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas incursion that caused about 1,200 deaths in southern Israel.

articles.title: 18 killed in Russian strikes in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia
articles.summary: Russian airstrikes killed at least 18 people in a village in southeastern Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region Monday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, condemning the attack as "utterl...
articles.full_text:
Russian airstrikes killed at least 18 people in a village in southeastern Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region Monday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, condemning the attack as "utterly horrific" and warning that the violence undermined hopes for progress toward peace.
Zelenskyy said Russian forces had repeatedly targeted the settlement with aerial bombs since the morning, striking a school being used as a humanitarian aid distribution center.
"Since this morning, the settlement has been hit several times by aerial bombs. The strikes targeted a school used for humanitarian purposes – people were receiving humanitarian aid there," Zelenskyy wrote on social media.
"Tragically, 18 people have already been reported killed," he added.
The Ukrainian president said the deadly bombardment further diminished prospects for diplomatic progress toward ending the war.
The attack came as Kyiv accused Moscow of exploiting a rare, U.S.-backed humanitarian cease-fire in the southern Kherson region last week to reinforce its military positions.
Nearly 800 people were evacuated from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky during a six-day pause in fighting, according to U.S. first lady Melania Trump, whom the White House credited with helping broker the arrangement.
Both Ukraine and Russia had previously welcomed the humanitarian initiative as a success.
However, Ukraine's General Staff alleged Monday that Russian forces used the temporary cease-fire to rotate troops, strengthen defensive positions and improve battlefield logistics.
"Under the ceasefire introduced for the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, units of the Defence Forces of Ukraine ensured that the ceasefire was observed and acted exclusively within the framework of the agreements reached," the General Staff said in a statement on X.
"The enemy, by contrast, used the humanitarian pause to improve its positions," it added.
The Kremlin did not directly confirm or deny the allegations.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said he had no specific information about troop movements during the cease-fire but described adjustments to military positions during such pauses as standard practice.
Peskov also suggested that Ukrainian forces had likely taken similar measures during the temporary halt in hostilities.
The competing accounts highlighted continued tensions between Moscow and Kyiv despite limited humanitarian cooperation, while the latest deadly strikes in Zaporizhzhia raised further concerns about prospects for a broader peace agreement.

articles.title: 9 killed as business jet crashes into Florida neighborhood
articles.summary: A business jet crashed into a residential neighborhood in South Florida, killing all nine people aboard and sparking a massive fire, as federal investigators prepared to provide an...
articles.full_text:
A business jet crashed into a residential neighborhood in South Florida, killing all nine people aboard and sparking a massive fire, as federal investigators prepared to provide an update Monday on the cause of the crash.
Video recorded by passersby captured the terrifying moment on Sunday afternoon when the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky before slamming into the ground and exploding in Green Acres, about 7 miles (11 kilometers) southwest of West Palm Beach. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as shocked residents looked on in horror. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
"Debris was everywhere. Debris hit my house. Everything was on fire. The road was on fire,” Anthony Blackmon, who lives near the crash site, told NBC affiliate WTVJ. "I’ve always seen it on the news, never thought it would happen so close to somebody like how it happened today.”
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed. Authorities have not released the names of the people who died.
Palm Beach County authorities were evacuating about 600 people from a nearby mobile home community while the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board investigate the crash.
Authorities have not provided any information about what caused the Bahamas-bound Learjet 60 to crash. NTSB officials planned to hold a news conference in West Palm Beach on Monday.
The jet began its journey at the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas, and airport spokesperson Jim Reynolds described it as a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on board.
The plane was heading east at 35,000 feet (about 11 kilometers) when the pilot started to report problems.
The pilot said ice was accumulating on the jet and that turbulence was jolting it by as much as 700 feet (213 meters), according to air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net . Rain pounded the region on Sunday.
"We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence,” the pilot told controllers.
The situation rapidly deteriorated.
The pilot requested permission to climb another 2,000 feet (about 610 meters) then quickly declared an emergency as the jet lost altitude at an alarming rate.
"We’re descending 8,000 - mayday, mayday - we’re descending 10,000 feet per minute,” the pilot radioed.
"We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute,” the pilot radioed, before delivering a devastating acknowledgment of what was about to happen. "We’re going to crash into the ground.”
The plane banked sharply to the right before crashing and exploding.
"It was a cataclysmic plane crash,” DeSantis told reporters at the scene. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road.”

articles.title: Iotova wins runoff to become Bulgaria's 1st elected woman president
articles.summary: Incumbent Iliana Iotova has won Bulgaria's presidential runoff by a clear margin, according to official results published Monday, making her the country's first elected woman presi...
articles.full_text:
Incumbent Iliana Iotova has won Bulgaria's presidential runoff by a clear margin, according to official results published Monday, making her the country's first elected woman president.
The former socialist EU lawmaker took first place with 57.5% of the vote, according to the figures. Challenger Andrey Gyurov, the candidate of the pro-Western liberal-conservative opposition camp, came second with 39.4%.
Iotova was backed by the center-left party Progressive Bulgaria, which governs alone. It remains to be seen whether she will be an effective check on the government of Prime Minister Rumen Radev.
The former journalist has held the presidency since January 2026, but has not yet been elected to it personally. When she was vice president, she temporarily took over the post after President Radev resigned to run in an early parliamentary election.
The war in Ukraine, close to Bulgaria's border, gave the election a foreign policy dimension. In recent weeks, drone attacks on merchant ships had increased in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea and in that of neighboring Romania. The pro-Western opposition urged the center-left government in Sofia to take a firmer line.
Iotova repeatedly campaigned for a peace settlement for Ukraine through negotiations with Russia. She said that she wanted to be a "president of peace" for Bulgaria. The newly elected president is due to take office on Jan. 22.
The 62-year-old Iotova will be Bulgaria's seventh head of state since the 1989 political changes. She is also the first woman to be directly elected by the people, which was seen in the Balkan country as a sign of emancipation. Iotova is also the commander-in-chief of the armed forces.
